title: Dashboard iteration framework & session provenance notes
content:
Purpose:
This note captures a compact, repeatable framework for iterating dashboards for inference surfaces (hosted API + dedicated). The emphasis: fast experiment-iterate cycles, bounded query-cost, and deterministic session provenance so oncall can reproduce incidents quickly.

Objectives:
- Define a small canonical metric set per surface (latency, tail-latency slices, kv-cache warmth, cold-start rate, percent-traffic-on-fallback model).
- Standardize span/trace anchors so session reconstruction ties tokens -> model shards -> route decisions.
- Introduce an iteration rubric (small experiment, probe, measure, prune) to keep dashboards lean.
- Add a lightweight query-cost budgeting step for each new widget.

Audience:
- Observability owners, SREs, serving-runtime engineers, product owners for rollouts.

Metric definitions (canonical set):
1) ttf-token-ms (time-to-first-token per request)
   - calc: p50/p90/p99 of time from request-received -> first-token-emitted
   - owner: eng-serving-runtime
   - alert: p99 > 800ms sustained 15m
   - notes: include network ingress delta only when tracing shows external-client span present

2) token-throughput-per-gpu
   - calc: tokens_emitted / active_gpu_seconds (per pool) per 5m window
   - owner: eng-platform-engineering
   - alert: drop >30% vs baseline over 1h
   - notes: required for dedicated capacity economics panels

3) kv-cache-warmth-index
   - calc: fraction of requests where kvcache_hit == true (session-scoped)
   - owner: eng-serving-runtime
   - alert: drop >10 percentage points for high-traffic tenants
   - notes: compute both per-tenant and global to detect cold-starting shards

4) model-fallback-rate
   - calc: count(fallback_to_variant) / count(total_requests) per 5m
   - owner: eng-routing
   - alert: >2% sustained for production tier
   - notes: trace should capture fallback_reason tag (OOM, latency_sla, routing_failed)

5) inference-error-rate (classed)
   - calc: errors by class (model-exec, runtime, input-validation) / total_requests
   - owner: eng-sre
   - alert: error-rate >0.5% and class == model-exec
   - notes: prioritize model-exec spikes with trace sample enrichment

Tracing and session provenance:
- Trace anchors: every request MUST include the following top-level tags: request_id, tenant_id, model_version, route_policy, kvcache_seed_hash, session_id (when present). These are small fixed-length tags to allow fast index lookups.
- Span naming: use stable verb-like names: request:receive, route:decide, model:load-weights, model:forward, output:emit. Avoid including dynamic values in span names.
- Sampling policy: adaptive sampling keyed by anomaly signals. Baseline: 1% global sampling. If a metric crosses a threshold (latency p99 spike, fallback-rate>threshold, token-throughput drop), increase sampling to 100% for the affected tenant+route for 10 minutes.
- Trace enrichment: for high-sensitivity sessions (billing tier, enterprise flag) always include full request payload hashes and kvcache trace diffs. Redact PII at span-attribute ingestion.
- Session reconstruction recipe: given a request_id -> follow request:receive -> route:decide -> model:forward spans and join on kvcache_seed_hash to collect cache events. Attach small snippet of prompt (first 256 chars hashed) to prevent exposing secrets.

Dashboard iteration framework (4 steps):
1) Hypothesis & minimal widget set:
   - Define the hypothesis (e.g., new batching kernel reduces p99 by >= 15% for long-sequence requests).
   - Pick 3–4 widgets: p99 latency by model_version, token-throughput-per-gpu, kv-cache-warmth, a probe histogram for sequence length distribution.
2) Cost bounding:
   - Estimate extra query cost for traces and high-cardinality widgets. Add an explicit budget note (e.g., +5k traces/day). Get signoff from SRE if budget > 10k traces/day.
3) Probe deployment & measurement:
   - Deploy probe (synthetic traffic or sampling instrumentation) for 48–72 hours. Use sparse bins for high-cardinality tags (tenant_id limited to top 10 tenants for initial run).
4) Prune & promote:
   - Remove widgets that generate >60% of query cost or provide redundant insight. Promote remaining widgets to the main oncall dashboard with owner and SLI thresholds.

Widget cost estimation heuristics:
- Rule of thumb: a timeseries with a small GROUP BY (model_version) is low cost. Any GROUP BY on tenant_id or model-shard-id is high-cardinality and costs ~5–10x.
- Traces attached to alerts should be limited by adaptive sampling windows.
- Maintain a dashboard-level comment documenting estimated daily query cost and trace-budget anchor.

Alert design guidance:
- Prefer multi-signal alerts: combine an SLI breach (e.g., p99 latency) with supporting context (kv-cache-warmth drop or model-fallback-rise) to reduce false positives.
- Severity mapping: Sev1 = total-tenant-impacted SLO breach; Sev2 = single-tenant critical SLO; Sev3 = investigative signals.

Ownership and runbook linkage:
- Each dashboard must include an Owners field (email alias) and a Runbook link. Example owners: obs-operators@redwood.com, runtime-owners@redwood.com.
- Runbooks should include: how to reconstruct session from trace, quick remediation steps (scale pool, revert rollout, patch kernel), and post-incident data collection checklists.

Practical instrument checklist (pre-rollout):
- Metric contracts defined and implemented (names, units, aggregation windows).
- Span tags present and validated on canary traffic (session_id, kvcache_seed_hash, model_version).
- Query cost estimate and SRE signoff if necessary.
- Dashboard owner assigned and runbook stub linked.

Quick experiments to try (short notes):
- Lightweight kvcache probe: instrument a 5% synthetic traffic probe that marks kvcache_seed_hash values; measure warmth index change per pool.
- Fallback attribution panel: stack fallback_rate by fallback_reason to determine systemic vs capacity-related fallbacks.
- Sequence-length heatmap correlated with p99 spikes to isolate long-seq slow-path regressions.

Open questions / unresolved
- How fine-grained should per-tenant dashboards be before we hit query-cost limits? Proposal: top-25 tenants by qps have dedicated tenant panels; others use aggregated rollups.
- Storage policy for trace payload diffs: keep diffs for 30 days for enterprise tenants, 7 days for open-hosted. Needs legal sign-off.

Next steps / action items:
- (INF-8342) Create a lightweight dashboard template (3 canonical widgets + owners + cost estimate) — owner: Samira. ETA: 2025-09-26.
- (PR #412) Add request_id and kvcache_seed_hash to the ingest pipeline trace schema — owner: Ethan. ETA: 2025-09-20.
- Run a 72-hour kvcache probe experiment on staging next week and collect warmth-index baseline — owner: Lina. ETA: 2025-09-22.

Notes on formatting for Drive doc: keep this doc as the single-source primer and link from iteration-specific docs (e.g., feature-rollout dashboards). If we iterate the rubric, keep changes small and date-stamped in the doc header.

Appendix: example wiggle-room thresholds (local defaults)
- latency p99: baseline * 1.25 over 30m -> page (if revenue-tier)
- kv-cache-warmth: drop 10pp over 1h -> investigate
- fallback-rate: >2% over 15m -> trigger triage

End of note.
